title: Overlapping bridges are skew or equivalent 3-bridges
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $C$ be a cycle in $G$, and let $e$ and $e'$ be edges of $G$ that do not lie on $C$; write $B$ and $B'$ for the bridges of $C$ containing $e$ and $e'$ respectively. If $B$ and $B'$ overlap, then either they are skew, or their sets of vertices of attachment to $C$ coincide and consist of exactly three vertices — that is, $B$ and $B'$ are equivalent $3$-bridges.
hypotheses_covered: $e$ is an edge of $G$ not on $C$
$e'$ is an edge of $G$ not on $C$
replaced:
\emph{If two bridges overlap, then either they are skew or else
they are equivalent 3-bridges.}
